Docker

2026-11-25

Source: vignettes/docker.Rmd
docker.Rmd

Docker

This guide shows how to build a Docker image with synapser 3.0.0 installed, starting from either the rocker/r-base image or the rocker/rstudio image.

What the image needs

R on Linux installs packages from source, so the image needs what is listed under Linux in the Installation vignette:

  • A C/C++ compiler. Most of synapser’s dependencies (such as reticulate, Rcpp, and rjson) contain compiled code. The rocker images already include one.
  • The libpng development headers (libpng-dev). The rocker images do not include them, and without them installing png fails with png.h: No such file or directory.

The image does not need Python. synapser 3.0.0 uses an environment that reticulate manages: the first time library(synapser) runs, reticulate uses uv to download a compatible Python and the Synapse Python client. Any Python you install with apt-get is left unused. See How synapser finds Python.

synapser 3.0.0 is installed from R-universe. RAN (http://ran.synapse.org) does not host synapser 3.0.0, so replace it with R-universe in any existing Dockerfile.

R image 

FROM rocker/r-base:4.6.1

# R installs packages from source on Linux. rocker/r-base already has the
# C/C++ compiler; the png dependency also needs the libpng headers.
# Python is not installed here: synapser 3.0.0 uses reticulate's managed
# environment, which downloads its own Python with uv.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get -y install --no-install-recommends libpng-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN R -e "install.packages('synapser', repos = c('https://sage-bionetworks.r-universe.dev', 'https://cloud.r-project.org'))"

Build and run it:

docker build -t synapser .
docker run -it --rm synapser R

RStudio image 

# This builds the rstudio docker image
FROM rocker/rstudio:4.6.1

# The png dependency needs the libpng headers if it is built from source.
# Python is not installed here: synapser 3.0.0 uses reticulate's managed
# environment, which downloads its own Python with uv.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get -y install --no-install-recommends libpng-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Must install and load synapser as rstudio since we are relying on
# the rstudio user to login.
USER rstudio
RUN R -e "install.packages('synapser', repos = c('https://sage-bionetworks.r-universe.dev', getOption('repos')))"
# when starting the container, it must run as root
USER root

reticulate caches the Python environment in the home directory of the user who first loads synapser. Install and load synapser as the user who will use it in the container (here rstudio), so that user reuses the environment created during the build. Any other user downloads it again on their first library(synapser). Switch back to root at the end, because the rocker/rstudio image must start as root.

Build and run it, then open http://localhost:8787 and log in as rstudio with the password you set:

docker build -f Dockerfile.rstudio -t synapser-rstudio .
docker run --rm -p 8787:8787 -e PASSWORD=<choose a password> synapser-rstudio

Logging in to Synapse from a container

Do not put your personal access token in the Dockerfile or the image. Pass it when the container starts instead, either as the SYNAPSE_AUTH_TOKEN environment variable:

export SYNAPSE_AUTH_TOKEN="your_personal_access_token"
docker run -it --rm -e SYNAPSE_AUTH_TOKEN synapser R

-e SYNAPSE_AUTH_TOKEN with no value copies the variable from your shell, so it must be set and exported there first. If it is not, Docker passes nothing and does not warn you. You can check with echo $SYNAPSE_AUTH_TOKEN before starting the container.

or by mounting your ~/.synapseConfig file into the home directory of the container’s user (/root for the R image):

docker run -it --rm -v ~/.synapseConfig:/root/.synapseConfig:ro synapser R

Either way, you still log in inside R. synLogin() with no arguments finds the token in the environment variable or the mounted config file:

library(synapser)
synLogin()

See the Authentication vignette for other ways to log in.
